end.summary:
Identified earthworm as living in soil and making tunnels.
Named ants and beetles as animals found in soil.
Initially classified earthworms as insects and said they spoil soil.
Later used zero legs to distinguish earthworms from six-legged insects, but the harmful/“yucky” belief remained.
Teach-back was not completed; lesson ended when Pihu asked to stop.
end.parentNote: Pihu practised naming animals in soil and comparing insects by their number of legs. They used the zero-legs clue to revise the classification of an earthworm, but still described it as harmful and yucky; this belief was not corrected by the end. At home, you can look at a picture of an earthworm together and discuss how its tunnels help air and water move through soil.
